questions.q: Who must decide, between which options, by when?
What is the headline figure and what does it measure?
What does the retrofit cost against the cap, and what happens if the decision slips?

good:
Tom, please approve Option A (retrofit both lines now), or choose B (Line 1 only) or C (wait until January), by Thursday the 14th.
Key figure: 92.4% pick accuracy at the pilot, up from 81%.
The vendor quotes $1.35M for the full retrofit against the $1.8M Q3 capex cap. If we miss Thursday the 14th the retrofit slot slips to November and we lose the rebate. Priya will execute if you sign off.

questions.q: Who must decide, between which options, by when?
What is the headline figure and what does it measure?
What does each option cost, and when is it done?

good:
Tom, please pick one of three downtown meter options by Wed Jan 15: replace all 420 meters now (Option A), replace only the 150 mechanical meters (Option B), or run a full study first (Option C).
Key figure: $180k to replace all 420 meters (Option A).
Option B costs $75k, done by Feb 15; Option C costs $12k and delays replacement to June. A 3% discount applies to A or B if we order before Feb 1.

questions.q: Who must decide, between which options, by when?
What is the headline figure and what does it measure?
What does each location cost, and how much budget is left?

good:
Dana, please choose the Austin location by Friday and approve the budget: 5th Street (Option A), the Domain (Option B) or near UT (Option C), since the lease option on the Domain spot is expiring.
Key figure: $2.1M annual revenue forecast for the best location.
A: 2,500 sq ft, $450K build-out, $12K monthly rent. B: 3,200 sq ft, $620K build-out, $15K rent, better foot traffic. C: 1,800 sq ft, $300K build-out, $9K rent, cheaper but smaller. This year's CapEx budget is $1.2M, with $380K already spent.

questions.q: Who must decide, between which options, by when?
What is the headline figure and what does it measure?
What does each option cost, and what must happen for the early install?

good:
Dana, please approve by Oct 30: rent 2 refrigerated trailers (Option A) or buy 2 used walk-in coolers (Option B) for the cold-storage overflow.
Key figure: 3,200 lbs of dairy per week turned away for lack of space.
Option A: $4,800/month, 3-month minimum, $14,400 total, delivered by Nov 12. Option B: $9,500 each plus $1,200 install, $20,200 total, installed by Nov 8 if we get the go-ahead by Nov 1. After your decision I coordinate with facilities.

questions.q: Who must decide, between which paths, by when?
What is the headline figure and what does it measure?
What does each path cost, what did energy do, and what is lost if the decision slips?

good:
Ana, please approve the budget line by March 14: roll out the hybrid dehumidification system to all five greenhouses by Q3, or pilot it in two more for another year.
Key figure: 41.7 kg/m² crop yield over the last 6 months, up from 38.2 kg/m² a year earlier.
Rollout costs $850k; the pilot costs $310k. The trial also cut energy use by 23%. After March 14 we lose the vendor discount.
